title.value: Findings of the 1st Shared Task on Multi-lingual Multi-task Information Retrieval at MRL 2023
title.justification: This paper provides the findings of a shared task focused on multi-lingual, multi-task information retrieval, which reflects the paper's goal and overarching theme.
title.quote: Findings of the 1st Shared Task on Multi-lingual Multi-task Information Retrieval at MRL 2023

extractions.description: This paper discusses the outcomes of a shared task on multi-lingual, multi-task information retrieval, highlighting the evaluation of large language models across multiple under-resourced languages. It introduces a novel benchmark that focuses on named entity recognition and reading comprehension in seven low-resource languages, aiming to enhance the applicability and fairness of information retrieval systems.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily addresses technical advancements and evaluations in natural language processing, specifically for information retrieval tasks. While it mentions fairness and applicability, it does not focus directly on climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our evaluation of leading LLMs reveals that, despite their competitive performance, they still have notable weaknesses such as producing output in the non-target language or providing counterfactual information that cannot be inferred from the context.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not align with any specific climate or ecological sustainable development themes. Its focus is on multi-lingual, multi-task information retrieval systems.
primary_category.quote: Our new shared task introduces a novel benchmark to assess the ability of multilingual LLMs to comprehend and produce language under sparse settings, particularly in scenarios with under-resourced languages.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address any additional themes related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: The shared task consists of two sub-tasks crucial to information retrieval: Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Reading Comprehension (RC).

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category within climate or ecological sustainable development that matches the content and focus of this paper, which is centered on language processing and information retrieval.
primary_sub_category.quote: With the advancement of language models accessing and processing vast amounts of information in different formats and languages, it has become of great importance to be able to assess their capabilities to access and provide the right information useful to different audiences.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development are applicable as the paper's scope is strictly within language processing.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: An important capability that enables responding to natural language questions with answers found in text.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce any new climate or ecological sustainable development category as it is unrelated to these areas.
new_primary_category.quote: We presented a new multi-lingual multi-task benchmark on information retrieval from Wikipedia in seven languages from typologically-diverse and low-resourced language families.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: As the paper is primarily focused on information retrieval and language processing, no new sub-category applicable to climate or ecological development is introduced.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: It is the system’s task to locate a suitable answer passage (if any).
